newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y., looks for council to approve deal.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y., looks for council to approve deal.

text.p: Troy, N.Y., which a rating agency has said will be in default if it defers a $1.4 million payment due Sept 15, expects its council to approve a separate refinancing, part of which it earlier rejected.
"We don't anticipate any problem in completing this portion of the financing," said Owen Goldfarb, Troy's budget director, Monday.

The city council last week rejected a plan to authorize the city to borrow $6 million to create a debt reserve and to pay for the costs of issuing new bonds through the Municpal Assistance Board (MAC).

New York state imposed the MAC on the city last year, when Troy was unable to sell its debt on its own. As soon as the council approves the new refinancing plan, the city hopes to soon issue new debt through the MAC.

And the city still is trying to avoid defaulting on the September 15 payment to three mutual funds, who own $35 million of debt that was issued under a lease back mortgage arrangement. "We really don't want to default, absolutely. That is not our intent," Goldfarb said, adding talks with the bondholders were continuing.
Troy, whose debt service in January totaled more than $9 million or 25 percent of its annual expenses, has said it does not have enough money in its reserve account to make the September 15 payment.
